subject: commitment
$comment: Computed values, made by two independent passes from PUBLIC-SPEC.md sections 2 and 3 alone. METHOD: fold purchases with c = keccak256(abi.encode(c, buyer, startIndex, endIndex)) from bytes32(0), where abi.encode of these static types is four 32-byte big-endian words, the address right-aligned in its word. Purchases are sorted by (block, logIndex) before folding. totalTickets sums endIndex - startIndex + 1. Every range case was checked to produce a different commitment under a half-open reading, and orderingWithinBlock was checked to differ when folded in file order rather than sorted order. PROVENANCE: Pass A: Claude (an AI), in Python with a generic keccak256 library, no implementation consulted. Claude also drafted part of the prose, so a disagreement was to be read as possible evidence the text is unclear, not only as a miscomputation. Pass B, 2026-09-28: a second person, on a separate machine, with no access to this file or to pass A's method, notes or terminal, in JavaScript with ethers v6 for keccak256 and ABI encoding. Different language and libraries on each side, so a shared library bug cannot make both passes wrong in the same way. All 8 values agreed exactly. Pass B raised four spec-text gaps, none of them contradictions, each fixed in PUBLIC-SPEC.md without changing any value: abi.encode word widths and the empty-round value (section 3), excluded-range inclusivity (section 6), the schema file as the normative field set per schemaVersion, and the complete-JCS-plus-validating-layer shape (section 9). Format: vectors/FORMAT.md.

cases.name: emptyRound
cases.description: No purchases. The commitment is its initial value and nothing is hashed.

cases.name: singleTicketAtZero
cases.description: One ticket at (0,0). Under a half-open reading this range is empty, so this case alone separates the two interpretations.

cases.name: singleFiftyTickets
cases.description: One purchase of 50 tickets, (0,49). totalTickets 50 confirms inclusive counting at a size where an off-by-one shows.

cases.name: adjacentRanges
cases.description: Two adjacent purchases, (0,9) then (10,19). Catches an implementation that leaves a gap or overlaps by one.

cases.name: manySmallPurchases
cases.description: Eight single-ticket buys from four distinct addresses, exercising the chaining of the running hash.

cases.name: oneLargeRange
cases.description: A single purchase of 5000 tickets. Confirms nothing iterates per ticket.

cases.name: sameBuyerNonContiguous
cases.description: Address A at (0,9), B at (10,19), A again at (20,29). Catches an implementation that groups or coalesces by address.

cases.name: orderingWithinBlock
cases.description: Three purchases in the SAME block with distinct log indices, listed here out of order. Ordering by block number alone is insufficient; log index within the block is required (section 2).
